newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania parliament appeals for NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania parliament appeals for NATO membership.

text.p: Lithuania's parliament on Thursday sent an appeal to NATO urging the alliance to include at least one Baltic state in a first round of enlargement.
Eighty of the 81 MPs present in the 138-seat house approved the appeal.
NATO is expected to name candidates to join the alliance at a summit in Madrid in July and the favourite candidates are Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
But the Balts, wary of huge neighbour Russia, say they are more in need of greater security than anyone.

"The parliament of Lithuania urges the governments of the NATO member states...to invite the Baltic states or at least one Baltic state to start NATO accession negotiations together with the first alliance candidates," the appeal said.
It said Lithuania was convinced the progress of the Balts, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, on the path of democracy and stability would be threatened if they were left out of NATO.
Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia believe that only NATO can shield them from a potentially hostile Russia, which has ruled them for most of the last 200 years.
Suspicion of Moscow runs deep in the small countries, which were annexed by the Soviet Union in 1941 after a brief period of independence.

Diplomats and analysts say the Balts have almost no chance of being invited for membership talks at the Madrid summit as Russia is fiercely opposed to NATO expansion and is particularly sensitive about the Baltic region.
However, the United States has repeatedly reassured the Balts that they will not be left in a security grey zone and that the door to NATO entry remains open for those who fail in a first round.
